test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
B, C, D, E, F, G and K are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. B sits third to the left of E. F sits second to

the left of C. Only E sits between K and F. D is not an immediate neighbour of B.

How many people sit between G and F when counted from the right of G?
solution:
Given, B, C, D, E, F, G and K are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre.

B sits third to the left of E.

Only E sits between K and F.

D is not an immediate neighbour of B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3a0431b0999d73ecc76dd4107371ef3a04169b96f01487dc0dd26d4fac30fbc6.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4867412db2cbbaf30422dcc524080196186268457c339ba77cd300e2313bfd5d.png] 

F sits second to the left of C.

And G sit at remaining place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6004aba3124755ab65b90e3ea67e15ace5ba3a5e993b5b61d95240a78b019a1e.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/520b1dff655a7582e5ed6f461d7573780691253b3da5c01d15033e234c972d67.png] 

So, Two people sit between G and F when counted from the right of G

Hence the correct answer is** "Option 3"**
